result.topic_en: Section 70 of Ramanujan's work on highly composite numbers, deriving the maximum order of the divisor function $\sigma_{-s}(N)$ by expressing $\log\Sigma_{-s}(N)$ asymptotically in terms of $\vartheta(x_1)$, $x_2$, and logarithmic-integral terms.
result.transcription:
Add Ms a 94$^{18\,(44)}$ (44) (88)
(370) $\Pi_{n-1}(x_{n-1})\,\Pi_n(x_n)\,\Pi_{n+1}(x_{n+1}) = \left|\frac{\zeta\{s(n-1)\}}{\zeta\{s(n+2)\}}\right| e^{O(x_1^{\frac{1}{n-1}-s})}$.
70. We shall now consider the order of $\Sigma_{-s}(N)$ i.e. the maximum order of $\sigma_{-s}(N)$. It follows from (317) that, if $3s \neq 1$, then
(371) $\Sigma_{-s}(N) = \Pi_1(x_1)\,\Pi_2(x_2)\,|\zeta(3s)|\,e^{O(x_1^{\frac{1}{3}-s})}$.
in virtue of (367), (369) and (370). But if $3s = 1$, we can easily show, by using (362), that
(372) $\Sigma_{-s}(N) = \Pi_1(x_1)\,\Pi_2(x_2)\,e^{O(\log\log x_1)}$.
It follows from §68 that
(373) $\log \Pi_1(x_1) = \log\left|\frac{\zeta(s)}{\zeta(2s)}\right| + Li\{\vartheta(x_1)\}^{1-s} - \frac{1}{2}Li\{\vartheta(x_1)\}^{1-2s}$
$+ \frac{1}{3}Li\{\vartheta(x_1)\}^{1-3s} - \cdots\cdots - \frac{(-1)^n}{n}Li\{\vartheta(x_1)\}^{1-ns}$
$- \frac{1}{2}Li(x_1^{\frac{1}{2}-s}) + \frac{x_1^{\frac{1}{2}-s} + S_s(x_1)}{\log x_1} + O\left\{\frac{x_1^{\frac{1}{2}-s}}{(\log x_1)^2}\right\}$,
where $n = [1+\frac{1}{2s}]$; and also that, if $3s \neq 1$, then
(374) $\log \Pi_2(x_2) = \log\left|\frac{\zeta(2s)}{\zeta(3s)}\right| + Li(x_2^{1-2s}) + O\left\{\frac{x_1^{\frac{1}{2}-s}}{(\log x_1)^2}\right\}$;
and when $3s = 1$
(375) $\log \Pi_2(x_2) = Li(x_2^{1-2s}) + O\left\{\frac{x_1^{\frac{1}{2}-s}}{(\log x_1)^2}\right\}$.
It follows from (371) — (375) that
(376) $\log \Sigma_{-s}(N) = \log|\zeta(s)| + Li\{\vartheta(x_1)\}^{1-s} - \frac{1}{2}Li\{\vartheta(x_1)\}^{1-2s}$
$+ \frac{1}{3}Li\{\vartheta(x_1)\}^{1-3s} - \cdots\cdots - \frac{(-1)^n}{n}Li\{\vartheta(x_1)\}^{1-ns}$
$- \frac{1}{2}Li(x_1^{\frac{1}{2}-s}) + Li(x_2^{1-2s}) + \frac{x_1^{\frac{1}{2}-s} + S_s(x_1)}{\log x_1} + O\left\{\frac{x_1^{\frac{1}{2}-s}}{(\log x_1)^2}\right\}$
where $n = [1+\frac{1}{2s}]$. But from (368) it is clear that, if $m > 0$, then
$Li\{\vartheta(x_1)\}^{1-ms} = Li\{\log N - x_2 + O(x_1^{1/3})\}^{1-ms}$
$= Li\left\{(\log N)^{1-ms} - (1-ms)x_2(\log N)^{-ms} + O(x_1^{\frac{1}{3}-ms})\right\}$
$= Li(\log N)^{1-ms} - \frac{x_2(\log N)^{-ms}}{\log\log N} + O(x_1^{\frac{1}{3}-ms})$

methods.what: Asymptotic for product of three consecutive Pi factors

Expansion of $Li\{\vartheta(x_1)\}^{1-ms}$ in terms of $\log N$ and $x_2$
